Jun Park: Heads-up: onboarding halcyon-50k-int4 hit a nondeterministic divergence around ~30250 tokens. Only reproducible when --kv-prefetch=on AND --scale-serialize=json (multi-shard). Repro below.

Jun Park: Repro command: `./serve_infer --model halcyon-50k-int4 --quant=int4 --kv-prefetch=on --rope-mode=adaptive-normalize --ctx=65536 --scale-serialize=json --shards=4 --seed=1234`

Jun Park: Short log excerpt from two shards:
```
[11:23:12] shard=0 pos=30249 rope_scale=1.000001234567 shard_scale_hex=0x3f800001
[11:23:12] shard=0 kv_write=30249 kv_read=30250
[11:23:12] shard=1 pos=30249 rope_scale=1.000001254321 shard_scale_hex=0x3f800002
[11:23:12] shard=1 kv_write=30249 kv_read=30251  <-- mismatch
```

Jun Park: The token diff looks like subword split + punctuation shift (deterministic across runs with same flags). If I switch `--scale-serialize=binary` or run single-shard, divergence disappears.

Marta R.: Interesting. Did you diff the serialized scale tables? JSON pretty-prints floats; maybe some shards write fewer sig-figs. If the runtime re-parses so that shard mappings differ slightly, that could shift kv_idx at large pos.

Jun Park: Yep. I pulled `scales_shard_*.json` from traces (trace id 1791000100). For pos 30249 the text representation differs at the 8th decimal.

Theo: Hypothesis: JSON uses standard double but our serializer casts to float32 to shrink payloads. Float32 rounding + adaptive-normalize's small fractional adjustments can produce different nearest-integer kv_idx after multiplication. Over many positions this causes a one-off at horizon boundary.

Theo: Quick mitigation: change serialization to fixed-point integers (store scale * 2**N as int) or increase decimal precision in JSON. Better: have an on-wire canonical representation (e.g., base64-packed int32) so deserialization is bit-identical across languages/shards.

Jun Park: I instrumented a simple Python comparator:
```
# loads scales_shard_0.json, scales_shard_1.json
for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(s0,s1)):
    if a != b:
        print(i, a, b, (a-b))
        break
```

Jun Park: It prints diff at pos 30249 with delta ~2.0e-08, but that tiny delta times pos yields index difference.

Marta R.: Can you try `--scale-serialize=json --scale-precision=12`? If it’s just text truncation, increasing precision might be a quick stopgap. But that's brittle and increases payload.

Jun Park: Tried `--scale-precision=12` locally; parity restored in my single-check. But fuzzbench still flagged one case in the matrix (rare).

qa-bot: Scheduling fuzz matrix: halcyon-50k-int4 (int4/int3), rope-modes (adaptive-normalize, clamp, linear), serialize (json,binary,compact64), horizons (4k/8k/16k). fuzz id fuzz-1791000201.

ops-bot: Trace/fuzz links: https://telemetry.internal/trace/1791000100 and https://telemetry.internal/fuzz/fuzz-1791000201 (ttl 7d).

Theo: I pushed a small prototype that encodes scales as int32 fixedpoint with N=24 (i.e., scale_int = round(scale * 2**24)) and serializes to compact base64. Runtime then uses same fixedpoint to compute kv_idx: `(pos * scale_int) >> 24`. This makes mapping bit-identical across all shards.

Marta R.: Can you bench perf impact? That extra multiply+shift in prefill path might matter at very high token rates.

Theo: Bench: added micros counter for mapping. Over a 1M-token prefill run the fixedpoint path adds ~0.45us/token on CPU prefill stage. On GPU-heavy online throughput it's negligible.

Jun Park: I ran the proto across 5 seeds and 3 shard counts; all passed (no diffs). Pushing traces to trace id above.

qa-bot: fuzz-1791000201 partial results: json-precision=12 still has 3/72 failures; fixedpoint-base64 encoding shows 0/72 failures so far. Full matrix running (eta ~2h).

deploy-bot: Recommendation: add a short-term canary: set default `--scale-serialize=binary` for hosted onboarding jobs for halcyon-50k-int4 and add a release note. If fixedpoint proves stable, prepare a backward-compatible migration plan for persisted serialized tables.

Marta R.: Also add unit tests: assert exact equality after serialize->deserialize roundtrip for scale arrays and a parity test `kv_idx(write)==kv_idx(read)` across shuffled shard reorderings. We should also add a compatibility flag to reject older serialized blobs that are text JSON without precision metadata.

Jun Park: I'll open a PR with: (1) fixedpoint base64 serializer, (2) --scale-precision flag with deprecation warning, (3) unit tests, (4) a small note in onboard checklist to run fuzzbench for serialize formats. Assigning to Theo for review.

Theo: I'll review and add CI job that runs the serialization parity test on PRs touching rope mapping code. Also will add a runtime switch `--rope-mapping=canonical-fixedpoint` behind a feature flag so we can rollout gradually.

deploy-bot: I'll schedule a canary that forces `--scale-serialize=binary` for current rolling onboarding until PR lands. Ping infra if you need emergency rollback.

Jun Park: Thanks all. Prioritizing as P2 for halcyon onboarding. Will post full fuzz results when available.
